title: Tokyo markets closed — year-end Market Holiday; Japan fixed income fully shut while US bonds run a half session
source: NEWS: jpx.co.jp/english/corporate/about-jpx/calendar/ ('Market Holidays', page's own 'Update : Feb. 06, 2026'), fetched direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, 33,103 bytes) and parsed date-by-date out of its 2026 panel by this session. The panel states 'JPX markets are closed on Saturdays, Sundays, national holidays, and on the dates indicated below' and its 2026 list ends with the entry **'Dec. 31 (Thu.) Market Holiday'**, immediately preceding the 2027 panel's 'Jan. 1 (Fri.) New Year's Day'. Note this is a JPX *Market Holiday* rather than a Japanese national holiday — the exchange's own year-end closure, listed alongside the national holidays under the same 'dates indicated below' clause; JPX's 2027 panel carries the identical 'Dec. 31 (Fri.) Market Holiday' entry, so the year-end closure recurs. INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED from a different primary the same day: SIFMA's holiday-schedule page (sifma.org/resources/guides-playbooks/holiday-schedule, HTTP 200, 298,926 bytes), parsed card-by-card with region attribution fixed to the page's own 'U.S. / U.K. / Japan Holiday Recommendations' section headings, carries in its **Japan** 2026 panel the card 'Bank Holiday' / 'Thursday, December 31, 2026' / (no early-close note) — i.e. a full recommended fixed-income close, not an early close. Filed estimate on three counts: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for a securities exchange's own holiday calendar, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and JPX's own note warns 'Exchange holidays are subject to change due to changes to national holidays under Japan's Act on National Holidays'. The DATE is not in doubt — the estimate label is about the taxonomy, not the evidence
notes: DISCOVERED during the sifma-bond-early-close-2026-12-31 initial research (2026-09-05), by parsing SIFMA's holiday schedule with correct REGION attribution rather than reading only its US panel. The sibling sifma-bond-early-close-2027-03-25 ledger parsed all 118 SIFMA entries but reported only the US ones, which is why this sat unfound. Why it earns a row: it makes 2026-12-31 the one dated session in the forward window where SIFMA's three regions are in three DIFFERENT states — US fixed income on a 2:00 p.m. ET early close, UK fixed income on a normal session (its panel carries no 12-31 card at all), and Japan fully shut. The practical consequence is sharper than the US early close it was found beside: a JGB or Japan-duration leg on 2026-12-31 is not shortened, it is UNAVAILABLE for the entire session, and after 14:00 ET that day the US cash bond tape and Tokyo are both dark while the US equity tape alone runs to 16:00. That matters on this date specifically because 2026-12-31 is crowded rather than empty — it also carries china-retaliation-suspension-expiry-2026-12-31 (medium, geopolitical), georgia-psc-data-center-cost-shift-2026-12-31 (medium) and nerc-computational-load-standards-2026-12-31 (low), one session after the confirmed fomc-minutes-2026-12-30. IMPACT LOW: a foreign-exchange closure moves nothing by itself, no house playbook is calendar- or holiday-keyed (docs/plans/trade-playbooks.md and docs/research/multi-symbol-sweep.md grepped this session for 'holiday|santa|year-end|closure|half-day|early close': zero hits in both), and this repo tracks no Japan-listed symbol. It widens caution about the 12-31 afternoon and licenses nothing. PRECEDENT: filed on the same shape as jpx-market-closure-2027-03-22, which the calendar already tracks. HONEST LIMIT: the UK 'normal session' reading in the discovering ledger is an absence-of-evidence inference from SIFMA's UK panel carrying no 12-31 card, and no UK primary was fetched to confirm it — that limit belongs to the sibling ledger's leg 6, not to this entry's own date, which rests on two independent primaries.
